archetype.name: Fringe Contender (run-first, QB-dependent)
archetype.definition: A .500 team whose playoff case depended on Lamar Jackson's arm and legs; with him on injured reserve, it has to tread water on Derrick Henry's carries and a defense that tackles well underneath but bleeds deep.

report.headline: Without Lamar, a .500 team with a leaky secondary must survive November.
report.take:
Baltimore is 4-4, last in an AFC North where everyone else has a winning record. The record is not a fluke in either direction. The point differential sits at -24, the wins it implies (4.2) match the wins it has, and the Ravens have covered only a third of their spreads, 27th in the league. The market has kept pricing them like the 2024 team that led the league in net EPA. They are closer to last year's 8-9 club: an offense around the top third, a defense around the bottom half, and a first-year staff under Jesse Minter still sorting out discipline.

The season splits on the quarterback. With Jackson healthy in the first month, the offense put up 41 in Indianapolis and 34 in Dallas, and the passing game carried games the run game didn't. Tyler Huntley's three starts produced one road win built on 208 rushing yards in Atlanta, then two losses in which the ground game fell apart: rushing EPA of -10 at Cleveland and -9.4 against Cincinnati. Defenses stopped respecting the pass and loaded up on Henry. Jackson's return in Buffalo was the worst game of the year: 91 passing yards, -20.2 passing EPA and three turnovers, followed by thumb surgery and injured reserve. Huntley is now 'probably' out with a toe sprain, and the only other quarterback on the report, Joe Fagnano, is limited with an ankle.

The numbers flatter the offense a little and the defense more than a little. Yards per game rank 8th, but much of that came in Jackson's good September. The defense's middling totals hide a sharp split. It is good at everything in front of it: short passes, tight ends, running backs, explosive runs. It is among the worst in the league at the deep ball and against opposing No. 1 receivers. Add the 29th-ranked penalty rate, line penalties 30th, and short-yardage conversion 30th, and this team keeps beating itself in small ways.

Where it goes from here depends on surviving the next month. After Jacksonville, the schedule eases with the winless Chargers, Carolina and Houston. Jackson's return estimate falls in mid-December, just ahead of four straight division games. If a backup can manage the soft stretch, Baltimore can still matter in January. If not, the division games become a spoiler run.

strengths.title: Henry-driven ground game and possession
strengths.body: Derrick Henry has taken the large majority of the carries, and the run game averages 4.36 yards a carry, 7th in the league. Combined with a staff that goes for it on fourth down more than anyone, Baltimore ranks 7th in time of possession and can shorten games. The catch is that this works best when the quarterback threatens defenses too. In Huntley's two losses the run game collapsed against stacked fronts, so expect this edge to shrink while Jackson is out.

strengths.title: Sound defense in front of it
strengths.body: Underneath, this defense is genuinely good. Short-pass EPA allowed ranks 8th, explosive runs allowed rank 4th, and running backs and tight ends have done little against it. It also hits quarterbacks at the 6th-best rate even though its overall pressure rate is middling, which points to interior push more than edge speed. This holds up as long as Roquan Smith (questionable, foot) stays on the field.

concerns.title: Quarterback room down to the studs
concerns.body: Jackson is on IR after thumb surgery with a mid-December estimate, and Huntley 'probably' won't play Thursday. Even before Jackson's injury, the Huntley version of the offense could not keep defenses honest; the run game cratered in two of his three starts. Jackson's Buffalo game may also have been the thumb talking. Either way, the offense is now built on whoever is healthy enough to take snaps.

concerns.title: Deep ball and WR1 exposure
concerns.body: This is a real structural flaw, not noise. Deep passes against Baltimore rank 27th in EPA allowed, and opposing No. 1 receivers produce the most EPA per target in the league against it. The defense also ranks 24th in takeaways, so the big plays aren't offset by turnovers. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins being out makes the back end thinner, not better.

concerns.title: Self-inflicted drive killers
concerns.body: Baltimore ranks 29th in penalties and 30th in line penalties. It converts short yardage at the 30th-ranked rate despite Henry and sits 24th in sack rate. Those are discipline and execution problems a new staff can fix, but the line is getting worse, not better. Olaivavega Ioane is out, and both Roger Rosengarten and John Simpson are questionable.

trend.note: A strong first month with Jackson gave way to a losing October under Huntley, then a 36-10 rout in Buffalo that ended with Jackson headed for surgery. The last two losses were by more than three touchdowns each.

nextGame.headline: Short week, likely a third QB, against a top-four Jaguars team
nextGame.body:
Jacksonville comes to Baltimore on Thursday at 5-2 with the league's second-best point differential per game and a top-five offense by EPA. Trevor Lawrence has started every game, and the Jaguars' passing EPA ranks 5th. Their defense is the problem for a Ravens offense that wants to run: it ranks 2nd against the run by EPA and 1st against short passes. The one soft spot is deep, where it ranks 29th. Offenses pass on it more than almost anyone in neutral situations, a sign that opponents find the run closed and throwing open. The Book has Jacksonville -8.5 with a 42.5 total, and Baltimore is +340 on the moneyline.

Availability tilts it further. Baltimore probably won't have Huntley, and Fagnano is limited with an ankle. Ioane is out on the line, with Rosengarten and Simpson questionable. Roquan Smith and Trey Hendrickson are questionable on defense, Hawkins is out at safety, and kicker Tyler Loop may go on injured reserve. Jacksonville has its own holes: both safeties Eric Murray (out for the season) and Antonio Johnson are out, DaVon Hamilton is done for the year, and Travon Walker, Jakobi Meyers and Bhayshul Tuten are all questionable. All of this lands on four days' rest.

waysToWin.title: Take shots at a depleted secondary
waysToWin.body: Jacksonville's deep defense ranks 29th by EPA, and opposing No. 1 receivers have done real damage against it. Now it is missing two safeties. If whoever starts at quarterback can push a few balls downfield to Zay Flowers, the run game gets the lighter boxes it hasn't seen since September.

waysToWin.title: Shrink the game and stay on schedule
waysToWin.body: A 42.5 total, a 7th-ranked time of possession and a staff that goes for it on every fourth down give Baltimore a path to a low-possession, coin-flip finish. That requires Henry to grind out manageable third downs even against an elite run defense, and the line to stop gifting penalty yards.

waysToWin.title: Make Lawrence live underneath
waysToWin.body: Jacksonville throws quickly, with time to throw ranking 26th, and Baltimore's short-pass defense is a top-10 unit. If the Ravens keep safeties deep and tackle the quick game, they can force long drives that a 4th-ranked red-zone offense still has to finish.

waysToLose.title: Offense stalls against the run wall
waysToLose.body: Jacksonville's run defense ranks 2nd by EPA and its short-pass defense 1st. That is exactly the menu a backup quarterback leans on. If the passing game can't threaten deep, this looks like the Cleveland and Cincinnati games, when the run game went deeply negative and the offense scored 13 or fewer.

waysToLose.title: Lawrence finds the deep holes
waysToLose.body: A top-five passing offense against the league's worst defense on WR1 targets and a bottom-six deep defense, minus Hawkins, is the matchup most likely to blow this open early. Once Baltimore trails by two scores, its run-first plan disappears.

waysToLose.title: Penalties and special teams leak points
waysToLose.body: A banged-up line that already ranks 30th in line penalties, plus special teams at 23rd in EPA with the kicker's status in doubt, hands a +0.8-per-game turnover-margin team the hidden yards it feeds on.

nextGame.watch: Whether Baltimore's quarterback, whoever it is, can complete anything 20-plus yards downfield against the safety-depleted Jaguars. Without that, Henry runs into the league's No. 2 run defense all night.

restOfSeason.body:
The good news is the calendar. After Jacksonville come the winless Chargers (32nd-ranked offense), Carolina and Houston, all beatable even with a backup if the run game and the underneath defense hold. Then Tampa Bay's 2nd-ranked defense, and four division games against teams that currently sit above Baltimore. Jackson's mid-December estimate lines up with that closing stretch, but it is an estimate after surgery, not a promise. A thumb on his throwing hand could limit him even when he's back.

What is sustainable: Henry's volume, the short-area defense and the clock control. What isn't: the September offense without Jackson. The penalty rate should come down some with a new staff, but the deep-ball problem has persisted all year and it is a personnel problem. Expect fewer points than the season average while the backups play and a defense that stays around league average, which makes eight or nine wins the realistic ceiling.
swingFactors: Jackson's thumb and actual return date
Whether a backup can make defenses respect the pass
Deep-ball defense in four closing division games

confidence.note: Eight games of data, but the quarterback situation has reset; backup-QB sample is three games and the next starter is unclear.
